title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem:
Read this booking handler from the makerspace assistant:

def handle(msg):
    slot = ask_model("Extract machine, date, time as JSON: " + msg)
    if not check_calendar(slot):
        return "Sorry, that slot is taken."
    book_slot(slot)
    send_email(slot)

How should you classify it?

options.text: An agent, since the model's output feeds the later steps
A workflow, since whatever the model returns, the next step is already set by this code
An agent, since it calls tools such as check_calendar
A workflow, since the model is called only once

items.stem: Every night a job reads the 500 new machine-usage log lines, which always have the same format, has a model summarize them, and stores the summary. The sponsor wants a predictable cost per night. Which design is best for this job?

options.text: An agent, since it can adapt if the log format changes
An agent, since it can re-check its summary until satisfied
A fixed workflow, since one pass gives a steady cost and output
A fixed workflow, since an agent could not summarize that many lines

items.stem: A fixed workflow answers each request with 2 model calls. An agent doing the same job averages 6 model calls per request, because it loops. Each call costs $0.003, and the assistant handles 1,000 requests. How many extra dollars does the agent cost compared with the workflow?

The assistant has two jobs. Job A: when a student confirms a booking, the sponsor requires the same checks every time and an audit log of each step. Job B: answer "why did my print warp?" from the manuals, where the number of lookups depends on what the student says. The sponsor caps every request at 8 model calls. Which design is best?

options.text: Job A as a fixed workflow; Job B as an agent loop capped at 8 calls
Both jobs as fixed workflows, with Job B always running three lookups
Both jobs handled by one agent, told by its prompt to log every step
Job A as an agent capped at 8 calls; Job B as a fixed workflow

items.stem: A pipeline runs three stages in code: classify, retrieve, draft. A fourth, final stage passes the draft to a model, and the code runs whatever word the model returns ("retrieve", "classify" or "stop") and repeats until it returns "stop". Which stage gives the model control over the flow?
